results.source_text:
@[simp]
theorem val_natCast (n a : ℕ) : (a : ZMod n).val = a % n := by
  cases n
  · rw [Nat.mod_zero]
    exact Int.natAbs_natCast a
  · apply Fin.val_natCast

results.name: ZMod
results.source_text:
/-- The integers modulo `n : ℕ`. -/
@[to_additive_dont_translate]
def ZMod : ℕ → Type
  | 0 => ℤ
  | n + 1 => Fin (n + 1)

results.name: ZMod.natCast_zmod_val
results.source_text:
/-- So-named because the coercion is `Nat.cast` into `ZMod`. For `Nat.cast` into an arbitrary ring,
see `ZMod.natCast_val`. -/
theorem natCast_zmod_val {n : ℕ} [NeZero n] (a : ZMod n) : (a.val : ZMod n) = a := by
  cases n
  · cases NeZero.ne 0 rfl
  · apply Fin.cast_val_eq_self
results.docstring:
So-named because the coercion is `Nat.cast` into `ZMod`. For `Nat.cast` into an arbitrary ring,
see `ZMod.natCast_val`.

results.name: ZMod.val
results.source_text:
/-- `val a` is a natural number defined as:
  - for `a : ZMod 0` it is the absolute value of `a`
  - for `a : ZMod n` with `0 < n` it is the least natural number in the equivalence class

See `ZMod.valMinAbs` for a variant that takes values in the integers.
-/
def val : ∀ {n : ℕ}, ZMod n → ℕ
  | 0 => Int.natAbs
  | n + 1 => ((↑) : Fin (n + 1) → ℕ)
results.docstring:
`val a` is a natural number defined as:
- for `a : ZMod 0` it is the absolute value of `a`
- for `a : ZMod n` with `0 < n` it is the least natural number in the equivalence class

See `ZMod.valMinAbs` for a variant that takes values in the integers.

results.name: ZNum.div_to_int
results.source_text:
@[simp, norm_cast]
theorem div_to_int : ∀ n d, ((n / d : ZNum) : ℤ) = n / d
  | 0, 0 => by simp [Int.ediv_zero]
  | 0, pos _ => (Int.zero_ediv _).symm
  | 0, neg _ => (Int.zero_ediv _).symm
  | pos _, 0 => (Int.ediv_zero _).symm
  | neg _, 0 => (Int.ediv_zero _).symm
  | pos n, pos d => (Num.cast_toZNum _).trans <| by rw [← Num.to_nat_to_int]; simp
  | pos n, neg d => (Num.cast_toZNumNeg _).trans <| by rw [← Num.to_nat_to_int]; simp
  | neg n, pos d =>
    show -_ = -_ / ↑d by
      rw [n.to_int_eq_succ_pred, d.to_int_eq_succ_pred, ← PosNum.to_nat_to_int, Num.succ'_to_nat,
        Num.div_to_nat]
      change -[n.pred' / ↑d+1] = -[n.pred' / (d.pred' + 1)+1]
      rw [d.to_nat_eq_succ_pred]
  | neg n, neg d =>
    show ↑(PosNum.pred' n / Num.pos d).succ' = -_ / -↑d by
      rw [n.to_int_eq_succ_pred, d.to_int_eq_succ_pred, ← PosNum.to_nat_to_int, Num.succ'_to_nat,
        Num.div_to_nat]
      change (Nat.succ (_ / d) : ℤ) = Nat.succ (n.pred' / (d.pred' + 1))
      rw [d.to_nat_eq_succ_pred]

@[simp, norm_cast]
theorem mod_to_int : ∀ n d, ((n % d : ZNum) : ℤ) = n % d
  | 0, _ => (Int.zero_emod _).symm
  | pos n, d =>
    (Num.cast_toZNum _).trans <| by
      rw [← Num.to_nat_to_int, cast_pos, Num.mod_to_nat, ← PosNum.to_nat_to_int, abs_to_nat]
      rfl
  | neg n, d =>
    (Num.cast_sub' _ _).trans <| by
      rw [← Num.to_nat_to_int, cast_neg, ← Num.to_nat_to_int, Num.succ_to_nat, Num.mod_to_nat,
          abs_to_nat, ← Int.subNatNat_eq_coe, n.to_int_eq_succ_pred]
      rfl

results.name: Sym.equivNatSumOfFintype
results.source_text:
/-- The `n`th symmetric power of a finite type `α` is naturally equivalent to the subtype of maps
`α → ℕ` with total mass `n`.

See also `Sym.equivNatSum` when `α` is not necessarily finite. -/
noncomputable def equivNatSumOfFintype [Fintype α] :
    Sym α n ≃ {P : α → ℕ // ∑ i, P i = n} :=
  (equivNatSum α n).trans <| Finsupp.equivFunOnFinite.subtypeEquiv <| by simp [Finsupp.sum_fintype]
results.docstring:
The `n`th symmetric power of a finite type `α` is naturally equivalent to the subtype of maps
`α → ℕ` with total mass `n`.

See also `Sym.equivNatSum` when `α` is not necessarily finite.

results.name: Equiv
results.source_text:
/-- `α ≃ β` is the type of functions from `α → β` with a two-sided inverse. -/
structure Equiv (α β : Sort*) where
  /-- The forward map of an equivalence.

  Do NOT use directly. Use the coercion instead. -/
  protected toFun : α → β
  /-- The backward map of an equivalence.

  Do NOT use `e.invFun` directly. Use the coercion of `e.symm` instead. -/
  protected invFun : β → α
  protected left_inv : LeftInverse invFun toFun := by intro; first | rfl | ext <;> rfl
  protected right_inv : RightInverse invFun toFun := by intro; first | rfl | ext <;> rfl
results.docstring: `α ≃ β` is the type of functions from `α → β` with a two-sided inverse.

results.name: Equiv.psigmaCongrRight
results.source_text:
/-- A family of equivalences `Π a, β₁ a ≃ β₂ a` generates an equivalence between `Σ' a, β₁ a` and
`Σ' a, β₂ a`. -/
@[simps (attr := grind =) apply]
def psigmaCongrRight {β₁ β₂ : α → Sort*} (F : ∀ a, β₁ a ≃ β₂ a) : (Σ' a, β₁ a) ≃ Σ' a, β₂ a where
  toFun a := ⟨a.1, F a.1 a.2⟩
  invFun a := ⟨a.1, (F a.1).symm a.2⟩
  left_inv := by grind
  right_inv := by grind
results.docstring:
A family of equivalences `Π a, β₁ a ≃ β₂ a` generates an equivalence between `Σ' a, β₁ a` and
`Σ' a, β₂ a`.

results.name: KroneckerDelta.kroneckerDelta_finSumFinEquiv
results.source_text:
/-- The Kronecker delta is invariant under the component-index equivalence `finSumFinEquiv`. -/
lemma kroneckerDelta_finSumFinEquiv (a b : Fin 1 ⊕ Fin 3) :
    kroneckerDelta (finSumFinEquiv a) (finSumFinEquiv b) = kroneckerDelta a b := by
  simp only [kroneckerDelta, Equiv.apply_eq_iff_eq]
results.docstring: The Kronecker delta is invariant under the component-index equivalence `finSumFinEquiv`.

results.name: Equiv.sumEquivSigmalCond
results.source_text:
/-- An alternative form of `Equiv.sumEquivSigmaBool` where `Bool.casesOn` is replaced by `cond`. -/
def sumEquivSigmalCond : Fin m ⊕ Fin n ≃ Σ b, cond b (Fin m) (Fin n) :=
  calc Fin m ⊕ Fin n
    _ ≃ Fin n ⊕ Fin m := sumComm ..
    _ ≃ Σ b, bif b then (Fin m) else (Fin n) := sumEquivSigmaBool ..
    _ ≃ Σ b, cond b (Fin m) (Fin n) := sigmaCongrRight (fun | true | false => Equiv.refl _)
results.docstring: An alternative form of `Equiv.sumEquivSigmaBool` where `Bool.casesOn` is replaced by `cond`.
